title: Iterative radix-2 divider off the EX critical path + single 33x33 multiplier
motivation:
The baseline Fmax is 5.4 MHz. The worst path (199.8 ns, 150 logic levels,
156 cells) runs forward_unit -> EX operand mux -> u_alu -> EX/MEM, i.e.
through the fully combinational 32-bit `/` and `%` operators in alu.sv.
Gowin synthesises each of DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU as a 32-stage ripple
subtract-and-select array, so the whole core runs at the speed of one
combinational divide. CoreMark (-O3) executes almost no divides in the
timed region (constant divides become multiplies), so paying ~33 cycles
per DIV costs close to nothing in iter/cycle while it removes the
dominant path. The next-deepest structure is alu.sv's three separate
64-bit products (mul_ss, mul_uu, mul_su: 6 DSPs plus a wide result mux),
which can be collapsed into one signed 33x33 product.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
1. New module rtl/divider.sv: a sequential radix-2 restoring divider on
   operand magnitudes (1 start cycle latching operands + 32 iteration
   cycles, one 33-bit subtract per cycle), producing quotient/remainder
   with RV32M sign fix-up. Special cases handled explicitly at start:
   divide-by-zero -> quotient all-ones (skip sign fix), remainder =
   dividend; INT_MIN/-1 falls out of magnitude arithmetic (quotient
   0x80000000, remainder 0) but may also be special-cased. Interface:
   start / op / a / b in, busy / done / result out; result held until
   consumed.
2. EX integration (ex_stage.sv): when ID/EX holds a valid DIV/DIVU/REM/
   REMU, the first EX cycle starts the divider with the POST-FORWARD
   rs1/rs2 values and latches them. While the result is not ready,
   `ex_busy` is asserted. On completion the EX/MEM register captures the
   divider result as alu_result and the LATCHED operands as rs1_val /
   rs2_val / write_data (forwarding sources will have drained by then, so
   the live forward muxes are stale; RVFI rs*_rdata must come from the
   latch). While ex_busy, EX/MEM captures a bubble (valid=0, ctrl='0 so
   reg_write/mem_read/mem_write are 0) — do NOT freeze EX/MEM like the
   dmem stall does, or a store/MMIO write in MEM would be re-issued
   every cycle. If stall_ex_mem (dmem stall) is also asserted, the
   divider keeps iterating but its done-result stays held until EX/MEM
   is allowed to capture; the done flag clears on that capture.
   alu.sv keeps only ADD..MULHSU; its DIV* arms go away (ex_stage muxes
   the divider result in for DIV-class ops).
3. hazard_unit.sv: new `ex_busy` input. ex_busy -> stall_if=1, stall_id=1
   (hold, NOT flush: gate flush_id with !ex_busy), EX/MEM bubble.
   Redirect cannot coincide (DIV is never a branch/jump).
4. RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS: the formal liveness check (checks_si.cfg,
   trig@10 / check@20) requires the next retirement within ~10 cycles, so
   under ALTOPS the divider must preload its counter to finish in 2
   cycles and output the ALTOPS formula ((a-b)^const) from the latched
   operands. This still exercises the whole multi-cycle stall/hold/latch
   handshake in formal; real arithmetic stays covered by test_alu.py,
   a new divider cocotb test and cosim.
5. alu.sv multiplier: replace mul_ss/mul_uu/mul_su with ONE product
   $signed({a[31]&a_signed, a}) * $signed({b[31]&b_signed, b}) (66-bit),
   a_signed = MULH|MULHSU, b_signed = MULH. MUL -> [31:0], MULH/MULHU/
   MULHSU -> [63:32]. Keep the ALTOPS arms byte-identical.
Measured ceiling (hypgen probe, `make timing TARGET=bench`, place option
0): with the DIV/REM arms stubbed out and the unified 33x33 multiplier,
Gowin reports Fmax 49.41 MHz (vs 5.44), 20 logic levels, logic 1971 LUTs
(vs 12312), DSP 2 (vs 6). New worst path (25.5 ns) is regfile -> ID ->
EX branch compare -> redirect -> IF/hazard -> ID/EX rs*_val, with the
regfile -> ALU -> dmem-address path right behind it. The real divider adds one
33-bit subtract per cycle plus a result mux into EX/MEM, well off that
path, so ~40-49 MHz is expected; CoreMark iter/cycle changes by <1% (a
handful of DIVs x 33 cycles). Fitness gain is ~8x, far above the 4.6%
acceptance bar; +50 is the schema cap, not the estimate. Implementer:
keep the divider result mux AFTER the EX/MEM capture decision (i.e. a
separate 2:1 in front of reg_q.alu_result), not inside the forwarded
ALU output that feeds redirect/dmem address.

title: Take M-ext off the EX critical path: iterative divider + MEM-stage multiplier
motivation:
Baseline Fmax is 5.44 MHz. The worst path, 199.8 ns through 150 logic levels
(MEM/WB.rd -> forward_unit -> ex_stage -> alu -> ex_stage/dmem), runs through
the purely combinational 32-bit `/` and `%` in alu.sv, with three separate
64-bit multipliers (mul_ss/mul_uu/mul_su) beside them. These sit behind the
forwarding mux in the same cycle as ADD/branch resolve. Every instruction pays
for the divider on every cycle, but CoreMark's timed region runs almost no
DIV/REM and only some MULs (mostly in matrix_mul / matrix_mul_const).
CoreMark/MHz is already about 2.23 (449k cycles/iter), so the score is limited
by Fmax, not IPC. Removing the ~150-level divider cone should raise Fmax by
roughly an order of magnitude, to the base-ISA limit set by forward-mux + ALU
+ branch compare + redirect (probably 40-70 MHz on GW2AR-18).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Restructure the M-extension datapath into two units outside the single-cycle
EX ALU:

1. Iterative divider (new rtl/divider.sv), radix-2 restoring/non-restoring,
   1 quotient bit per cycle (~33-34 cycles). It works on operand magnitudes,
   then fixes signs: quotient negated if the signs differ, remainder takes the
   dividend's sign. Divide-by-zero is a special case: quotient = all ones,
   remainder = dividend, for both signed and unsigned. INT_MIN / -1 comes out
   right from the magnitude algorithm (0x80000000 / 1 -> 0x80000000 after
   negation, remainder 0), but add a unit test for it. The divider latches its
   forwarded operands on the first cycle a DIV/DIVU/REM/REMU sits in ID/EX. While
   busy it raises `div_busy`: the hazard unit holds PC and ID/EX
   (stall_if/stall_id) and EX/MEM captures a bubble (valid=0, reg_write=0,
   no mem op) each cycle. On `done`, EX/MEM captures the div result as
   alu_result and the pipeline advances. A `done_q` flag stops the divider
   from restarting while the same instruction is still held by a coincident
   dmem stall (stall_ex_mem must still take precedence and hold EX/MEM; the
   finished result stays latched until EX/MEM accepts it). Under
   `RISCV_FORMAL_ALTOPS` the divider keeps the same busy/done handshake but
   finishes after a short fixed latency (1-2 cycles) and returns the ALTOPS
   formulas ((a-b)^const per op). This keeps the stall path formally checked
   within the BMC depth and keeps liveness tractable.

2. Multiplier moved to the MEM stage (new rtl/multiplier.sv). Use one 33x33
   signed multiply instead of three 64-bit products. Sign-extend each operand
   by a per-op bit: MULH a,b signed; MULHSU a signed, b unsigned; MULHU/MUL
   unsigned. Then select [31:0] or [63:32]. Operands come straight from the
   EX/MEM register's existing post-forward rs1_val/rs2_val fields, so the
   path is register -> DSP -> mux -> MEM/WB register, with no forwarding mux
   in front. Gowin can absorb the EX/MEM operand flops into the DSP input
   registers. mem_stage writes the product into MEM/WB.alu_result when
   ctrl.is_mul is set, so the existing WB mux and MEM/WB->EX forwarding carry
   it unchanged. The hazard unit treats MUL like a load: if ID/EX holds a MUL
   whose rd matches the IF/ID rs1/rs2, insert one bubble (extend the
   load_use term to `(mem_read | is_mul)`). EX/MEM->EX forwarding of a MUL is
   then never needed. The ALTOPS MUL formulas move to the multiplier module
   under the same `ifdef`.

3. alu.sv keeps only the RV32I ops (ADD..LUI). Remove its M cases and all
   three products so the EX cone becomes forward mux -> adder/shifter/logic
   -> branch compare -> redirect.

Expected: IPC barely moves, maybe -1..-3%, from MUL-use bubbles in the matrix
kernels and the rare 34-cycle divide. LUT count drops sharply (the
combinational divider is most of the 12.3k LUT4). Fmax should rise from 5.4
MHz to tens of MHz, several times the current fitness. The schema caps the
delta at +50%, and even very conservative Fmax outcomes clear that.

title: Fetch-stage bimodal BHT + static JAL prediction (zero-bubble taken branches, no BTB)
motivation:
The core always predicts not-taken: every taken conditional branch and
every JAL/JALR costs a 1-cycle bubble (EX redirect flushes the one
F/D instruction). Because this core has no IF/ID register (the PC reg
drives imem and the returned word is decoded in the same cycle), the
full instruction is available in the fetch cycle, so a direction
predictor needs NO BTB: the target is simply pc + B/J-immediate.

Measured on the actual scored binary (bench/programs/coremark.elf,
-O3, 2K, 10 iterations, between the 0x10000100/0x10000104 markers,
via test/cosim/reference.py): 2.92M instructions; conditional
branches 18.1% (55.6% taken), JAL 1.69%, JALR 0.47% (all returns).
Baseline redirect bubbles = 0.124 per instruction. Baseline CPI from
fitness (12.12 iter/s at 5.442 MHz -> 449K cycles/iter, 292K
instr/iter) is ~1.54, so redirects are ~8% of all cycles.
Simulated predictor miss rates on this trace: static BTFN 21%,
bimodal-64 9.7%, bimodal-128 9.2%, bimodal-256 8.2%,
bimodal-512 7.4%, gshare-1K 7.2%. Bimodal-256 + always-taken JAL
leaves 0.0196 bubbles/instr (JALR kept unpredicted); adding a RAS
would only reach 0.015 (+0.3% more), not worth the complexity.

Fmax is set by the 200 ns combinational divider path (u_fwd > u_ex >
u_alu), so a small fetch-side predictor does not move Fmax today, and
its fetch path is flop-sourced (imem data is a register in the timed
bench) so it stays cheap once the divider is pipelined.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a fetch-stage direction predictor verified in EX:
1. New rtl/branch_predictor.sv: 256-entry x 2-bit bimodal BHT
   (saturating counters, synchronous reset to weakly-taken 2'b10 so
   Verilator/formal start deterministic), read combinationally with
   index pc[9:2] of the PC register (in parallel with the imem
   access), one write port driven from EX.
2. In if_stage, pre-decode imem_data: pred_taken = slot not
   flushed/NOP'd AND ((opcode == BRANCH && BHT[pc[9:2]][1]) ||
   opcode == JAL) AND imm[1] == 0 (instr[8] for B-type, instr[21]
   for J-type; PC is always word-aligned, so this is target[1] and
   we never fetch a misaligned target that EX would trap without
   redirect). pred_target = pc + imm_{B|J} (dedicated adder fed
   directly from instruction bits, not from imm_gen). PC priority:
   reset > EX redirect > stall(hold) > pred_target > pc+4.
   JALR is never predicted (keeps today's 1-cycle penalty).
3. Carry pred_taken through if_id_t -> id_ex_t (cleared on
   flush/bubble). In ex_stage: actual_taken = (branch_taken ||
   is_jump) && !misalign_fault; redirect = in.valid &&
   (actual_taken != in.pred_taken); redirect_target = actual_taken ?
   (is_jump ? jump_target : branch_target) : pc + 4. A correct
   predicted-taken needs no target compare because fetch computed the
   same pc+imm. Any pre-decode false positive (e.g. reserved BRANCH
   funct3 decoded illegal) is repaired by the pred=1/actual=0
   redirect to pc+4, so correctness never depends on the predictor.
   EX/MEM pc_next and every RVFI field are unchanged (still derived
   from the actual outcome), so riscv-formal pc_fwd/pc_bwd/liveness
   remain the correctness proof.
4. BHT update from EX for valid conditional branches only
   (ctrl.is_branch && valid), gated with !stall_ex_mem so a
   dmem-stalled branch trains exactly once; counter moves toward
   branch_cond. Hazard unit keeps flush_if/flush_id on `redirect`
   (which now means mispredict), and redirect keeps priority over
   stall in if_stage exactly as today.
Expected: redirect bubbles 0.124 -> ~0.020 per instruction, i.e.
~0.104 of ~1.54 CPI = ~6.8% fewer cycles per iteration at unchanged
Fmax -> ~+7% fitness. Cost ~+300-450 LUT and ~+512 FF (or LUTRAM) on
a 12.3k-LUT design that has ~8k LUT headroom.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Pure timing changes; CoreMark cycle count should stay exactly the same, so
all of the gain comes from Fmax.
(1) Force the regfile out of BSRAM (`(* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *)`
on `regs`; fall back to "registers" if Gowin ignores it or the reset loop
blocks inference). The async read + write-first bypass then happen in ID,
before a real ID/EX DFF. EX paths launch from a flop (tC2Q ~0.4 ns instead
of 2.26 ns) and lose the 2 bypass/fix-up LUTs, saving ~3.5 ns on both
tied paths.
(2) Take redirect out of the ID capture cone. Now that the regfile read
happens in ID, the redirect -> NOP mux -> regfile address path would
otherwise lengthen. The decoder, imm_gen, regfile addresses and load-use
compare all use RAW imem_data. Slots are killed only through flush_id
(= (load_use | redirect | imem_stall) & !dmem_stall & !ex_busy), which
sync-clears only ID/EX ctrl + valid. The data fields (rs?_val, imm, pc,
instr, rd, rs?_addr) get CE = !stall with no reset/flush, because a bubble
has ctrl='0 and valid=0, so its data is don't-care. This is
cycle-equivalent to today: ID/EX never captures while redirect=1 (either
flush or dmem-stall hold, and a DIV in EX can't redirect). A spurious
load-use from garbage imem_data during imem_stall or redirect still gives
the same single bubble.
(3) Registered forwarding match bits. In ID compute m_ex = (ID/EX.rd ==
rs, rd != 0) and m_mem = (EX/MEM.rd == rs, rd != 0) for rs1 and rs2 and
latch them with the ID/EX data (same CE). In EX the select is
(m_ex_q & EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write) ? EXMEM : (m_mem_q & MEM/WB.ctrl.reg_write)
? MEMWB : RF. The live reg_write qualification keeps misalign-trap and
divider-bubble cases exact. The matches are valid whenever ID/EX
captures, because EX/MEM and MEM/WB only advance together with ID/EX or
freeze together under dmem_stall. They go stale only for a DIV held under
ex_busy, whose operands are already latched in the divider. This removes
the 5-bit compare from both paths.

motivation:
After the iterative divider (hyp-001, 49.9 MHz) two different cones sit at ~26-27 ns
and each masks a fix to the other one:
  (a) hyp-001's worst path: regfile BSRAM (it absorbs ID/EX.rs1_val) -> forward mux ->
      33x33 DSP multiply -> ALU op mux -> EX/MEM.alu_result, which Gowin folds into the
      dmem BSRAM address register (15 cells, 27.0 ns).
  (b) hyp-002 (MUL moved to MEM, 48.5 MHz): regfile -> forward mux -> branch compare ->
      redirect -> if_stage NOP-mux on instr -> hazard_unit load-use compare on the
      *muxed* instr -> stall_id/flush_id -> synchronous reset/enable of the whole ~200-bit
      ID/EX register (44 cells, 26.1 ns).
hyp-002 moved only the multiplier. That exposed (b) at the same delay, so Fmax did not
move, but it cost only +0.8% cycles (4.528M vs 4.492M). Neither cone alone is worth
fixing. Both have to be cut in the same change, and the EX loop has to be shortened
enough that the next path is clearly shorter. Both cones share the same EX-stage
structure: every operand goes through one forward mux that feeds a single wide result
mux, and redirect is serialised through the fetch word and fans out to every
pipeline flop.

A. Predictor with a registered redirect.
1. New rtl/branch_predictor.sv: 256 x 2-bit bimodal BHT, reset to 2'b10.
   Read index is the fetch PC register pc[9:2], so the read is flop-sourced and
   runs in parallel with the imem access. One synchronous update port.
2. if_stage pre-decodes imem_data.
   pred_taken = slot valid (not flushed, imem ready)
                && ((opcode==BRANCH && BHT bit1) || opcode==JAL)
                && target[1]==0,
   where target[1] is instr[8] for B-type and instr[21] for J-type.
   pred_target = pc + B/J immediate, from a dedicated adder on the raw
   instruction bits (not through imm_gen).
   PC priority: reset > redirect_q > stall(hold) > pred_target > pc+4.
   JALR is not predicted.
   pred_taken travels in if_id_t and id_ex_t, and is cleared on flush/bubble.
3. ex_stage computes
   actual_taken = (branch_taken || is_jump) && !misalign_fault and
   mispredict = in.valid && !redirect_q && (actual_taken != in.pred_taken).
   No redirect or flush is driven combinationally from EX any more. mispredict
   is captured into a new EX/MEM.mispredict bit. A correct predicted-taken needs
   no target compare, because fetch computed the same pc+imm.

   redirect_target = ex_mem.pc_next, which already holds the resolved next PC

   stall can never hold it in EX/MEM and redirect_q lasts exactly one cycle. In

     its BHT training are all gated by !redirect_q.

title: Flatten EX: one-hot AND-OR result mux, shared add/sub/SLT adder, rs1+imm AGU, registered WB forward, 2-LUT redirect
motivation:
I ran `make timing TARGET=bench` on the champion (hyp-20260928-001-r2s0,
158.22, 70.6-71.1 MHz). Three different path families are tied within
0.5 ns of the 19.46 ns worst arrival (about 14.1 ns of data after the
5.33 ns clock insertion):
 A. mem_to_reg -> WB mux -> fwd -> DSP MUL -> ex_result -> dmem hold mux
    -> dmem BSRAM ADB (paths 1, 3-5, 7-18). Gowin moves EX/MEM.alu_result
    into the dmem BSRAM address register, so every EX result producer is
    in the dmem-address cone, although a dmem address is only rs1 + imm.
 B. EX/MEM.reg_write -> fwd select LUT (fanout 13) -> 2 fwd mux LUTs ->
    alu_a -> ALU carry chain -> SEVEN LUT levels
    (ex_result_27_s14/s13/s10/s6/s3/s1/s0) -> EX/MEM.alu_result_27
    (path 6, 19.43 ns). The chain SUM leaves at 13.81 ns, and the
    op-case mux, base_result and the MUL mux cost 5.6 ns after it. So an
    AGU alone would move Fmax by less than 0.1 ns.
 C. mem_to_reg -> WB mux -> 2 fwd LUTs -> branch compare carry chain ->
    4 LUTs (branch_op case, taken, misalign, redirect) -> PC CE LUT ->
    u_if/pc CE (paths 19, 20, 25, 19.02 ns).

alu_result) plus a 3-LUT forward. The r2s0 lesson says to fix every
near-critical path together, or the next one simply takes over.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
These are pure logic-depth changes. The CoreMark cycle count stays at
4,491,817 cycles, so the whole gain comes from Fmax.
(1) Registered, pre-muxed WB forward. MEM computes result =
mem_to_reg ? load_data : alu_result and latches it into a new
MEM/WB.result (held on hold_wb like the other data fields; only valid
clears). The regfile write data, fwd_mem_wb and RVFI rd_wdata all read
this flop. This removes 1 LUT and a fanout-64 net from A, B and C.
(2) Dedicated AGU. ex_stage adds agu = rs1_fwd + imm (its own carry
chain) and latches it into a new EX/MEM.mem_addr. mem_stage takes
dmem_addr, byte_mask, mem_misalign, the load shift and the RVFI
aligned_addr from mem_addr, not alu_result. The MUL, shifter, logic
unit and result mux all leave the dmem cone, which fixes A.
(3) Flat one-hot EX result, decoded in ID. The decoder emits registered
one-hot/unit controls in place of the 5-bit alu_op case:
  - sel_add. One shared 33-bit adder does ADD/SUB/SLT/SLTU. In the
    alu_b mux LUT, b is inverted by sub (alu_src ? imm : rs2) ^ sub,
    with cin = sub. Operands are sign- or zero-extended to 33 bits by a
    registered signed bit, so slt = sum[32].
  - sel_slt: bit 0 only.
  - logic_op[1:0]: 00 = off, then AND, OR, XOR. This is one LUT4 per
    bit whose output is already 0 when unused.
  - sel_shift + shift_dir/arith: a single shifter fed from rs1 (no
    pc/auipc mux).
  - sel_side: a register-sourced value precomputed in ID and latched in
    ID/EX (side = LUI imm, AUIPC pc+imm, or JAL/JALR link pc+4). In EX
    it is only (is_div ? div_result : side_q), which starts at flops.
    Because AUIPC is computed in ID, alu_a = rs1 always and the auipc
    mux leaves the adder input.
ex_result = OR of the gated unit outputs, then is_mul ? mul : that as
the LAST level. That is 2 LUTs after the adder SUM instead of 7, which
fixes B. The ID adder that computes pc+imm is shared with the branch/JAL
target, latched as ID/EX.target.
(4) 2-LUT redirect. Branch conditions come from the eq / lt / ltu flags
of the compare, which uses the registered one-hot conditions
(cond_eq, cond_lt, cond_ltu, cond_inv) decoded in ID:
  cond = ((eq & c_eq) | (lt & c_lt) | (ltu & c_ltu)) ^ c_inv.
Misalignment is known in ID for branches and JAL: the target is
pc + imm with an aligned pc, so misaligned iff imm[1]. ID latches
br_ok = is_branch & !imm[1] and jal_ok = is_jal & !imm[1]. Only JALR
needs jalr_sum[1] = rs1[1] ^ imm[1] ^ (rs1[0] & imm[0]), which is 1 LUT
after fwd. The results are:
  redirect = (br_ok & cond) | jal_ok | (is_jalr & !jalr_sum[1])
  redirect_target = is_jalr ? {jalr_sum[31:1], 0} : target_q
The trap semantics stay identical: a taken misaligned branch or a
misaligned jump sets is_illegal, clears reg_write and suppresses the
redirect, and pc_next = pc+4. The trap/pc_next logic only feeds EX/MEM
flops, off the PC CE cone. This fixes C.
(5) Optional fanout relief. If the report still shows the fanout-74
EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write or the fanout-13 fwd select nets, duplicate the
registered reg_write qualifier (per rs1/rs2 forward use) or add
syn_keep/syn_preserve copies.
Estimate. The paths become:
  B: ~13.3 ns chain + 2 LUTs, about 15.1 ns arrival.
  A (MUL -> 1 LUT -> EX/MEM flop): about 15.2 ns.
  C (compare chain + 3 LUTs): about 15 ns.
Next up are the unmeasured ID-side paths (imem BSRAM -> decode ->
LUT-RAM read -> ID/EX, and load-use -> stall CE), which I expect at
about 15-16 ns. That gives roughly 82-90 MHz, about +15-25% at the same
IPC.

title: Write back from MEM: kill the MEM/WB->EX forward path, 1-LUT EX forward mux, ID bypass of MEM result, dedicated AGU
motivation:
The champion (hyp-001-r2s0, 158.22, 71.07 MHz, 2.23 CoreMark/MHz) is now
purely Fmax-bound: the cycle count is already at the core.yaml per-MHz
target, so every percent of fitness has to come from the clock.
Its worst path (19.46 ns arrival, 9 cells) is
  MEM/WB.ctrl.mem_to_reg flop -> u_wb mem_to_reg mux (w_data)
  -> EX 3:1 priority forward mux (two AND-qualified selects = 2 LUT levels)
  -> mul sign-extend LUT -> DSP (~3.8 ns) -> hi/lo + ex_result mux
  -> dmem BSRAM address input (the EX/MEM.alu_result flop is retimed into
     the BSRAM's input register, so the path ends at the BSRAM setup).
Every other EX path (ALU -> EX/MEM, branch compare -> redirect -> PC /
flush) begins with the same WB mux + 3:1 forward mux prefix: ~3 LUT
levels and 3 routes (~3 ns of the 14 ns period) spent only on choosing
where an operand comes from. The textbook 5-stage keeps a second forward
source (MEM/WB) only because the regfile is written one stage late.
Earlier lessons say to fix the prefix on the distributed-RAM regfile base
without pipelining MUL (MUL pipelining costs cycles); this hypothesis
removes the prefix structurally instead of registering it.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Change the pipeline topology so the regfile is written at the END OF MEM
(4-stage write-back: IF, ID, EX, MEM/WB), leaving exactly one forwarding
source into EX, and move the dmem address onto its own adder.

1. MEM-stage write-back. reg_file write port is driven from MEM:
     w_en   = EX/MEM.valid & ctrl.reg_write & !mem_misalign & !dmem_stall
     w_addr = EX/MEM.rd
     w_data = mem_to_reg ? load_data (aligned/extended dmem_rdata)
                         : EX/MEM.alu_result
   dmem_stall (= !dmem_ready & mem_op) gates the write so a held LOAD
   writes exactly once, on the cycle its data arrives.
2. ID-stage write-first bypass (already in reg_file) now bypasses the MEM
   write data into the ID/EX operand register. This covers every
   producer at distance >= 2, including the load-use case: LOAD in MEM

title: Zero-bubble fetch prediction on the champion: LUT-RAM bimodal BHT + pre-decoded B/J targets, registered recovery PC
motivation:
The champion (hyp-001-r2s0, 158.22) runs exactly the baseline cycle count
(4,491,817 cycles vs 4,491,485). Every taken branch and every JAL/JALR still
costs one bubble because the redirect comes from EX while IF/ID is a single
combinational stage. The only predictor data point so far is misread in
LESSONS.md. hyp-003-r1s2 (fetch BHT + static JAL on the same 1-cycle-redirect
pipeline shape) cut cycles from 4,491,485 to 4,193,149, which is 7.1% more
IPC. Its fitness only rose 4.1% because the divider-bound Fmax moved by
seed noise (5.44 -> 5.29 MHz). That gain was never ported onto the
divider-free, distributed-RAM-regfile champion.
The champion's worst path is MEM/WB mem_to_reg -> WB mux -> fwd mux ->
DSP MUL -> ex_result -> dmem BSRAM address, 19.46 ns. Fetch prediction adds
no logic to that path. The fetch-side logic launches from flops (PC reg,
and the LFSR-driven io_imemData in fpga/core_bench_si.sv) and has several
ns of slack. So the IPC gain should carry straight through to fitness if
the redirect cone is kept as deep as it is now. r1s2 did not do that: its
redirect target mux was selected by the late actual_taken bit. r1s2 also
built the BHT as 512 reset flops plus a 256:1 read mux (+1086 LUT, +513 FF).
This design avoids both problems.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Add a fetch-stage direction predictor with exact pre-decoded targets.
Mispredict recovery stays the existing 1-cycle combinational EX redirect,
and its target comes from a register.

1. BHT: 256 x 2-bit bimodal counters in distributed LUT-RAM
   ((* syn_ramstyle = "distributed_ram" *), no reset, `initial` fill to
   2'b01 weakly-not-taken for sim determinism). It has one async read port
   indexed by the fetch PC reg pc[9:2] and one synchronous write port.
   The 2-bit counter read at fetch travels down the pipe with the
   instruction (ID/EX.bht_ctr). EX computes the saturating inc/dec from
   branch_cond, and the write is REGISTERED: upd_en/upd_idx/upd_ctr flops
   are written into the BHT the next cycle. branch_cond then only reaches a
   flop D input, never the LUT-RAM write port. Stale-counter races in tight
   loops only cost accuracy, never correctness.
2. Fetch pre-decode from raw imem_data (the same bits ID decodes):
   is_jal = opcode 1101111. is_br = opcode 1100011 && funct3 not 2 or 3
   (only legal encodings are predicted). The J/B immediate is muxed by
   is_jal, and pred_target = pc + imm uses a single adder.
   pred_taken = imem_ready && (is_jal || (is_br && bht_rd[1])) && !imm[1],
   so a misaligned target is never predicted and the existing EX misalign
   trap handles it.
   next_pc = redirect ? redirect_target
           : stall ? pc
           : pred_taken ? pred_target
           : pc + 4.
   redirect stays the last mux level, so its depth to the PC D pin is
   unchanged. PC advance (!stall_if && !redirect) is exactly the condition
   under which ID/EX captures a valid instruction, so the pred bit latched
   into ID/EX is always the prediction that steered the PC.
3. Registered recovery PC: IF computes alt_pc = pred_taken ? pc+4 :
   pred_target (both already computed there) and ID/EX latches it with the
   data fields (CE only). pred_taken is cleared with ctrl/valid on
   flush/reset so a bubble can never redirect. In EX:
   redirect_target = is_jalr ? {jalr_sum[31:1],0} : alt_pc_q. This removes
   the in.pc + in.imm adder and the is_jump mux from the branch
   redirect-target path.
   redirect = !misalign_fault && ((is_branch && (branch_cond ^ pred_q)) ||
   is_jalr || (is_jump && !is_jalr && !pred_q) ||
   (pred_q && !is_branch && !is_jump)). The last term is defensive.
   branch_cond still enters only one LUT before redirect, the same depth
   as today's is_branch && cond.
   pc_next, rd_wdata, the misalign trap and all other RVFI-feeding logic
   keep their current actual-outcome definitions. That logic is pruned
   from the timed netlist anyway.

Expected result. Cycles drop to about 4.19M (-6.6%, the r1s2 measurement
on an identical redirect structure): correctly predicted taken branches
and all JALs become free, and mispredicts keep the current 1-cycle cost.
Fmax should stay at about 71 MHz because nothing is added to the MUL ->
dmem worst path or to the redirect -> PC/flush_id cone. The fitness
estimate is 158 * 1.07 = about 169 (+6..7%).
Do NOT register the redirect. r2s2 shows that costs about 1.3% of cycles
(4.25M vs 4.19M), and redirect is not the champion's worst path.

title: Kill the MEM/WB->EX forward (resolve it in ID) and trim one LUT off each tied EX tail
motivation:
`make timing` on the champion (r3s0) shows five paths within 0.05 ns of each
other (16.51-16.55 ns, 88.8-90.8 MHz), and ALL of them start at a MEM/WB
forward-source flop:
  1. MEM/WB.ctrl.reg_write -> fwd select LUT -> 3:1 fwd mux (LUT4+MUX2_LUT5)
     -> DSP multiplier -> MUL select LUT -> EX/MEM.alu_result   (7 cells)
  2. MEM/WB.result -> fwd mux -> branch compare carry chain -> br_cond LUT
     -> redirect LUT -> PC next/CE                               (39 cells)
  3. MEM/WB.result -> fwd mux -> shared add/sub/SLT carry chain -> unit-OR
     LUT -> MUL-select LUT -> EX/MEM.alu_result                  (38 cells)
The shared prefix (live select qualification + a 3-source mux, whose
select nets fan out to 64 LUTs) and one post-carry LUT in each tail are the
removable pieces. Fixing only one of the tied paths does not move Fmax
(lesson from r2s0: fix every near-critical path together).

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Three coordinated cuts, zero cycle-count change for CoreMark:
(A) Remove MEM/WB as an EX forward source. While instruction I is in ID its
    two-ahead producer sits in EX/MEM and its final write value is
    mem_stage's combinational `result`. ID captures
      ID/EX.rs?_val <= (rs?_m_mem && mem_wen_next) ? mem_result : rf_rs?_data
    (mem_wen_next = EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write && !mem_misalign, exported by
    mem_stage). ID/EX only captures on edges where EX/MEM and MEM/WB also
    advance (dmem stall, ex_busy and load-use all hold ID/EX), so this is
    exactly the value the old MEM/WB forward supplied; the regfile
    write-first bypass still covers the MEM/WB producer. EX then needs
      rs = (rs_m_ex_q && EX/MEM.ctrl.reg_write) ? EX/MEM.alu_result : rs_val_q
    = ONE LUT4 per bit straight off flops (no select LUT, no MUX2_LUT5).
    The live reg_write term keeps JALR-misalign traps and divider bubbles
    correct as today. Duplicate the qualify flop per operand to cut fanout.
    -> path 1 loses a LUT + MUX2 + a high-fanout hop; paths 2/3 lose the MUX2.
(B) Branch tail: precompute in ID registered "take-if" bits
    (take_eq, take_ne, take_lt, take_ge from br_ok/br_sel, plus
    always_take = jal_ok) so redirect = always_take | (lt ? T1 : T0) | jalr
    term, where T1/T0 are a 1-LUT function of eq and the take bits; the
    carry-chain lt output then drives a single LUT before the PC D/CE and
    the flush, instead of br_cond LUT -> redirect LUT.
(C) ALU tail: reorder the EX result OR so the adder output enters the LAST
    LUT: ex_result = (sel_add & sum) | rest, with
    rest = is_mul ? mul : (slt | logic | shift | side). The adder path
    keeps 1 LUT after the carry chain (was 2); the MUL path gains back one
    LUT at its tail but lost ~1 LUT + MUX2 at its head in (A), so it stays
    balanced.
Expected: each tied path loses ~0.8-1.2 ns (16.55 -> ~15.5 ns, ~+6-7%
Fmax) with identical CoreMark cycles. New ID-side cost is one 2:1 level
after the LUT-RAM read/bypass and a dmem BSRAM -> align -> result ->
ID/EX path of ~4-5 LUTs after tC2Q, both expected well under 15 ns.

title: Zero-bubble fetch prediction on the flattened-EX champion: LUT-RAM bimodal BHT, prediction folded into the ID-registered branch select, no new logic after the compare chain
motivation:
The champion (hyp-001-r3s0, 202.12, 88.8/90.8/90.8 MHz) still runs the baseline
cycle count, 4,491,817 cycles. Every taken branch, JAL and JALR costs one bubble,
because the redirect comes out of EX while IF/ID is one combinational stage.
hyp-003-r3s2 measured the IPC side of zero-bubble fetch prediction with a LUT-RAM
bimodal BHT, pre-decoded B/J targets and the same 1-cycle mispredict redirect:
4,193,175 cycles, which is -6.65% cycles and +7.1% IPC. It was built on the OLD r2s0
base and lost about 6% Fmax (71.1 -> 66.7 MHz), with +517 LUTs. Its fitness only
broke even, so the IPC win has never been banked.

I ran `make timing` on the r3s0 champion (place option 0, 88.8 MHz). Three
families are tied at about 11.2 ns of data delay:
  1. MEM/WB.reg_write -> forward select -> DSP MUL -> EX/MEM.alu_result
     (7 cells).
  2. MEM/WB.result -> 2 forward LUTs -> 32-cell lt-compare carry chain ->
     branch-cond LUT (ctrl_with_trap.reg_write_s7) -> u_if n69_s24 -> n69_s12
     -> n69_s5 -> n328_s0 -> PC CE, on all 32 pc bits (39 cells).
  3. MEM/WB.result -> forward -> shared adder -> EX/MEM.alu_result.
Any predictor that adds even one LUT between the compare chain and the PC or
ID/EX flush, as r3s2's `br_cond ^ pred_q` did, loses Fmax one-for-one against
the +7% IPC.
Everything else a predictor needs is flop-to-flop with lots of slack in the
timed wrapper. io_imemData is an LFSR flop and io_imemAddr only feeds the LED
XOR, so the fetch pre-decode -> pc+imm adder -> next-PC path starts at a flop
and ends at the PC flop, at about 7 ns against the 11 ns period.

hypothesis.hypothesis:
Fetch-stage direction prediction with exact pre-decoded targets. The only EX
change is re-encoding registered bits, so the redirect cone after the compare
chains stays one LUT to the redirect plus one LUT to the PC CE / flush.
1. New rtl/branch_predictor.sv: a 256 x 2-bit bimodal BHT in distributed
   LUT-RAM (syn_ramstyle "distributed_ram", no reset, `initial` fill 2'b01).
   - Async read indexed by the PC flop pc[9:2].
   - The write port is REGISTERED. EX drives upd_en/upd_idx/upd_ctr into
     flops that write the RAM one cycle later, so branch_cond only ever reaches
     flop D pins.
   - Staleness in tight loops costs accuracy only, never correctness. r3s2
     measured exactly this scheme.
2. IF/ID (one combinational stage), pre-decoding the raw imem_data:
   - is_jal = opcode 1101111.
   - is_br = opcode 1100011 && funct3 is neither 2 nor 3, the same legality
     rule as the decoder.
   - pred_taken = !imm[1] && (is_jal || (is_br && bht_rd[1])).
     It is not gated by imem_ready: an imem stall already holds the PC and
     flushes the slot.
   - Reuse ID's existing target = pc + imm adder (imm_gen output) as the
     predicted target. No second adder.
   - PC flop: CE = redirect | adv, where adv = !stall_if comes from flops
     only; D = redirect ? redirect_target : (pred_taken ? target : pc + 4).
     Redirect stays the last D level and still overrides every stall.
     Collapse today's 4-LUT CE tail so redirect reaches CE through ONE LUT
     (CE = LUT(br_mis, jalr_go, adv)).
3. ID/EX: fold the prediction into registered control, with no EX-side XOR.
   - mis_sel = br_sel ^ {1'b0, pred_taken}. Flipping br_sel[0] turns
     eq<->ne and lt<->ge, so cond(mis_sel) = actual_cond XOR pred.
   - jal_go = jal_ok & !pred_taken. This is always 0 by construction; keep it
     only as a defensive, flop-sourced term.
   - recov = pred_taken ? pc + 4 : pc + imm is a new CE-only 32-bit field.
     ID/EX.target is then read only by RVFI pc_next and gets pruned, so the
     net flop count is unchanged.
   - Carry bht_ctr[1:0] and pred_taken (flush/reset-cleared like ctrl/valid)
     for the update and RVFI-invisible bookkeeping.
4. EX:
   - redirect = (br_ok & cond(mis_sel, eq, lt)) | (is_jalr & !jalr_bit1)
                | jal_go.
     The logic depth is the same as today's (br_ok & cond(br_sel)).
   - redirect_target = is_jalr ? {agu[31:1],0} : recov_q, the same 2:1 as
     today.
   - pc_next, the misalign trap, rd_wdata and every RVFI field keep their
     actual-outcome definitions, using the true br_cond from br_sel and
     target_q, so formal pc_fwd/pc_bwd are unaffected.
   - BHT update: upd_en = valid & is_branch & !stall_ex_mem, idx = pc[9:2],
     ctr = saturating inc/dec of bht_ctr_q toward the actual br_cond.
5. hazard_unit logic is unchanged. flush_id still ORs redirect, which now
   means "mispredict or JALR". The PC advances without a redirect exactly when
   ID/EX captures a valid slot, so the latched pred bit is always the one that
   steered the PC. That holds even across load-use and dmem-stall re-reads,
   where the BHT may have been updated in between.
Expected results:
- Cycles: about 4.19M (-6.65%, the r3s2 measurement on this exact redirect
  and pipeline shape; r3s0's cycle count equals r2s0's).
- Fmax: within noise of 90.8 MHz. Paths 1 and 3 are untouched. Path 2 keeps
  one LUT after the compare chain before redirect and loses about 3 LUTs of
  CE tail, so it gains slack that absorbs the extra D-mux level for
  pred_target.
- Area: roughly +150-250 LUTs (16 RAM16 plus a read mux, a 32-bit recov mux,
  pred D-mux levels), versus r3s2's +517.
- Fitness: about 202 * 1.07 = 216.
